# Core Intersections

An intersection is generated around a center point where two or more roads meet. Its geometry has three parts:

* the **road surface** in the middle, a flat polygon textured with the intersection's road texture (or with a road's own intersection texture);
* the **crosswalks**, a textured quad at the end of each road with a crosswalk size greater than 0;
* the **junctions**: one road-like strip between each pair of consecutive roads (going clockwise), typically sidewalks, curbs and railings, generated by the core like a short road.

Optionally, **extra terrain pieces** add surfaces spanning all the junctions (MM2 uses them for the walls and gallery ceilings of tunnels).

An intersection type is a folder in `elements/intersections/<type>/`:

```
intersections/<type>/
├── ui.json
├── parameters.json
├── settings.json
├── junctions/<roadTypeA>_<roadTypeB>.json
└── components/<component>.json          (or in elements/sharedComponents/)
```

## Size and placement

The program computes how far each road stops from the center so that the road edges do not overlap (using the `totalWidth` getter of the roads, the width on the ground for a banked end; the end of a road can also be skewed by its yaw, and raised by its connection height), then adds the road's crosswalk size, its intersection size increase and the intersection's `sizeIncrease`. Roads are sorted clockwise around the center; for each pair (I, J) of consecutive roads, the junction of type `<type of I>_<type of J>` is used.

## `parameters.json`

Same format as for roads (see [Parameters and UI](Parameters-and-UI)). The parameters and definitions of the intersection type are also visible in all its junctions. Required definitions:

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `uMult`, `vMult` | UV scale of the road surface and of the extra terrain pieces, whose UVs are the world X and Z coordinates multiplied by these values. |

Built-in state properties (edited in `mainGroup`): `type`, `sidewalkSegments` (number of segments of the junction curves), `sizeIncrease`.

## `settings.json`

```json
{
    "roadTexture": "texture1",
    "defaultCrosswalkTexture": "texture2",
    "roadStartCrosswalkTexture": "startCrosswalkTex",
    "roadEndCrosswalkTexture": "endCrosswalkTex",
    "extraTerrainPieces": [ ... ]
}
```

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `roadTexture` | Name of the intersection parameter holding the road surface texture. A road can override it with its own start/end intersection texture. |
| `defaultCrosswalkTexture` | Name of the intersection parameter holding the crosswalk texture. |
| `roadStartCrosswalkTexture`, `roadEndCrosswalkTexture` | Names of road **getters** returning the road's own crosswalk texture for its start and end; if the road's value is not empty it is used instead of the default (optional). |
| `extraTerrainPieces` | Optional list (default empty), see below. |

## Junction files

A junction file describes the strip between road A (the first road clockwise) and road B (the next one). It works like a road type whose curve goes from the end of road A to the end of road B, around the corner.

```json
{
    "standardFloatsBoolsAndInts": ["totalWidth", "roadWidth"],
    "standardVec3s": [],
    "standardVec2s": [],
    "sectionVertices": ["totalWidth", "roadWidth", "0"],
    "roadSplineVertex": 1,
    "actualSegments": "if(notDefaultTex, 1, segments)",
    "importedParameters": [
        { "fromStart": true,  "name": "sidewalkHeight", "type": "vec3", "newName": "A_swh" },
        { "fromStart": false, "name": "sidewalkHeight", "type": "vec3", "newName": "B_swh" }
    ],
    "staticDefinitions": [ ... ],
    "dynamicDefinitions": [ ... ],
    "textureDefinitions": [
        { "name": "rail_texture1", "options": ["rail_A_texture1", "rail_B_texture1"], "index": "rail_texIndex" }
    ],
    "anchors": ["v0+swhAnchor"],
    "textures": ["texture0", "rail_texture1"],
    "texturesMapping": { "intersectionSidewalk": [0], "rail_rail_left": [1] },
    "components": [
        { "name": "intersectionSidewalk", "condition": "A_hasRealSidewalks or B_hasRealSidewalks" }
    ],
    "extraTerrainSplines": [
        { "name": "wall", "vertex": "v0-localUp+localRight*(rail_height/3)" }
    ]
}
```

| Key | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `standardFloatsBoolsAndInts`, `standardVec3s`, `standardVec2s` | yes | Names of road [getters](Core-Roads#standard-getters) read from each road and available as variables in `sectionVertices` (only there). |
| `sectionVertices` | yes | Float expressions: lateral distances of the junction section vertices from the road's center line, measured on each road end. They are **full** widths: the program multiplies them by half of the road's left vector, so `totalWidth` is the outer edge. At least two entries are needed (the section direction is taken from `v0` to `v1`). These expressions can only use the standard getters listed above, `segments` and `notDefaultTex`. |
| `roadSplineVertex` | yes | Index of the section vertex that marks the edge of the road surface: the road surface polygon follows the curve of this vertex, `ground` below it. |
| `actualSegments` | yes | Float expression: the number of sections of the junction (normally `segments`, which comes from the intersection's `sidewalkSegments`). |
| `importedParameters` | no (default empty) | Values copied from the two roads: `fromStart` true for road A, false for road B; `name` is a parameter or definition of the road type, `newName` the variable name in the junction; `type` is `float`, `int`, `bool`, `vec2`, `vec3` or `texture` (a texture is copied into the junction's state, so it can be used in `textures` and `textureDefinitions`). Values missing from the road's type are 0/false/empty. Import parameters or static definitions: dynamic definitions hold whatever value the road's last section left. |
| `staticDefinitions`, `dynamicDefinitions` | no | Added after the intersection type's own definitions. Late definitions are not supported in junctions. |
| `textureDefinitions` | no | Chooses a texture among several state properties: the junction state property `name` is set to the value of `options[index]`, `index` being a float expression. |
| `anchors` | no | Anchor lines along the junction (vec3 expressions). Needed whenever the roads have anchors. They must start and end exactly (within 1 cm) on the corresponding anchors of the two roads, so that the anchor chains connect and terrain patches can follow them around the corner. |
| `components` | yes | As for roads; components are looked up in the intersection type's `components` folder, then in `sharedComponents`. |
| `textures`, `texturesMapping` | yes | As for roads, but the texture names refer to the junction state (intersection parameters, imported textures, texture definitions). |
| `trafficLanes`, `propsLines` | no | Parsed but not generated for junctions yet. |
| `extraTerrainSplines` | no | For each extra terrain piece, the vertex (vec3 expression) the piece passes through at each junction section. |

### Missing junctions

If the junction for a pair of road types is missing, the program uses the junction of road A's type with itself, then road B's, then any junction of the intersection type, and logs a warning. Providing a junction for every pair of road types that can meet avoids surprises.

### Junction variables

Available in junction expressions, besides the intersection parameters and definitions, the imported parameters and the junction's own definitions:

| Variable | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `worldUp`, `worldRight`, `worldForward` | vec3 | World axes. |
| `totalLength` | float | Length of the junction (measured between the midpoints of `v0` and `v1`). |
| `segments` | float | Number of sections. |
| `z`, `segment` | float | Distance along the junction and section index (from 1). |
| `ground` | float | Height difference between the junction vertices and the road surface at this section (the `height` getter of the roads, interpolated). |
| `localUp`, `localRight`, `localForward` | vec3 | Section frame; `localRight` points from `v1` to `v0`. |
| `v<n>`, `absX<n>`, `absY<n>`, `absZ<n>` | | Section vertices and their world coordinates. |
| `v<n>_0`, `v<n>_1`, `localRight0`, `localRight1`, ... | | First and last section. |
| `thisIsEndA`, `thisIsEndB` | bool | Whether the intersection is at the end (rather than the start) of road A / road B. Useful because "left" and "right" parameters of a road swap depending on which end meets the intersection. |
| `convex` | bool | Whether the corner between the two roads is convex. |
| `selfIntersectingSpline` | bool | Whether the junction curve intersects itself (roads too close, with negative size increases). |
| `notDefaultTex` | bool | Whether one of the two roads uses its own intersection texture. |

The order of evaluation and the component format are the same as for roads (see [Core Roads](Core-Roads#component-files)).

## Extra terrain pieces

```json
{
    "name": "wall",
    "junctionCondition": "hasWall",
    "junctionConditionMode": "or",
    "parametersSourceIndex": "0",
    "splineOverride": true,
    "facingUp": false,
    "uMult": "1",
    "vMult": "1",
    "texture": "rail_texture5",
    "textureSource": "junction",
    "condition": "wall_active and (not gallery_active or wall_index < gallery_index)"
}
```

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `name` | Name of the piece; also the name of the `extraTerrainSplines` entry in the junctions. |
| `junctionCondition` | Name of a boolean variable of the junctions, evaluated for each junction. |
| `junctionConditionMode` | How the junction results are combined: `or` (at least one), `and` (all), `xor` (exactly one). |
| `parametersSourceIndex` | Float expression: which of the matching junctions provides the parameters (index into the list of junctions where the condition is true). |
| `splineOverride` | If true, the piece's spline is computed with the source junction's state for every junction (so all the sides use the same parameters, for example the same wall height). |
| `facingUp` | Whether the surface faces up (floor) or down (ceiling or wall seen from inside). |
| `uMult`, `vMult` | Float expressions: UV scale of the piece (combined with the intersection's `uMult`/`vMult`). |
| `texture`, `textureSource` | Name of the state property holding the texture, read from the source junction's state (`junction`) or from the intersection's state (`intersection`). |
| `condition` | Boolean expression on the intersection variables deciding whether the piece is generated. Two variables are available for every piece: `<name>_active` (the combined junction condition) and `<name>_index` (the index of the source junction), which allow choosing between pieces (as in the MM2 example above, where the wall and the gallery exclude each other). |

The piece is a polygon through the spline vertices of all the junctions, triangulated like the road surface.
